blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:

The caller workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are a **ceiling** for a called reusable workflow. Per GitHub docs ("Reusing workflows"):

> The GITHUB_TOKEN permissions passed from the caller workflow can be only downgraded (not elevated) by the called workflow.

This is not theoretical for this repo — `ai-teammate.yml` documents the exact failure mode from a live 2026-10-03 incident: *"a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails"*.

Re-verified live this pass: the canonical `factory-sm-merge-guard.yml` (awf#31, merged to `@main` 2026-10-13T06:14Z) declares on its `guard` job:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
```

and writes the deduplicated `sm-guard` alarm issue with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` — which is exactly the token this stub caps at `contents: read`.

Consequence if merged as-is: when the guard detects an invariant violation (its entire reason to exist), the `gh api` issue write gets **403**, the designed self-diagnosing alarm issue is never filed, and the only signal is an opaque red run — precisely the confusion the alarm issue exists to explain. The stub breaks the feature's failure path.

**Fix** — grant what the called job needs. This mirrors the sibling stub `factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which grants the canonical kicker's full permission set (`actions: write`, `contents: read`, `pull-requests: read`, `checks: read`):

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue is filed by the called workflow
```

Note: the repo-wide `test_workflowLint.js` duplicate-key scan stays green either way; this is purely a token-scope contract with the called workflow.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Add `workflow_dispatch` for an on-demand smoke test** (fourth pass; still applicable — file unchanged)

The stub fires only on push to main, so the first real execution of this wiring happens on the next main landing — a bad time to discover a contract mismatch. Adding a manual trigger lets you dispatch the stub on demand (on main it asserts the current head tree against the last SM validation, a harmless no-op when green):

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

This matches the sibling `factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which also exposes `workflow_dispatch` alongside its automatic triggers. On a `workflow_dispatch` event `github.event.head_commit.id` is empty and the canonical script falls back to `github.sha`, so the called guard handles this event shape correctly (verified in the live `factory-sm-merge-guard.yml`: `ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}`).

# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).

# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.

and writes the deduplicated `sm-guard` alarm issue with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` — which is exactly the token this stub caps at `contents: read`.

  contents: read

```

Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothi…

blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,

blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Stub permissions starve the guard's alarm path — `issues: write` missing** (fifth pass; the head bump is only a main-merge — the workflow file itself is still unchanged since round 1)

The caller workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are a **ceiling** for a called reusable workflow. Per GitHub docs ("Reusing workflows"):

> The GITHUB_TOKEN permissions passed from the caller workflow can be only downgraded (not elevated) by the called workflow.

This is not theoretical for this repo — `ai-teammate.yml` documents the exact failure mode from a live 2026-10-03 incident: *"a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails"*.

Re-verified live this pass: the canonical `factory-sm-merge-guard.yml` (awf#31, merged to `@main` 2026-10-13T06:14Z) declares on its `guard` job:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
```

and writes the deduplicated `sm-guard` alarm issue with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` — which is exactly the token this stub caps at `contents: read`.

Consequence if merged as-is: when the guard detects an invariant violation (its entire reason to exist), the `gh api` issue write gets **403**, the designed self-diagnosing alarm issue is never filed, and the only signal is an opaque red run — precisely the confusion the alarm issue exists to explain. The stub breaks the feature's failure path.

**Fix** — grant what the called job needs. This mirrors the sibling stub `factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which grants the canonical kicker's full permission set (`actions: write`, `contents: read`, `pull-requests: read`, `checks: read`):

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue is filed by the called workflow
```

Note: the repo-wide `test_workflowLint.js` duplicate-key scan stays green either way; this is purely a token-scope contract with the called workflow.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Add `workflow_dispatch` for an on-demand smoke test** (fifth pass; still applicable — file unchanged)

The stub fires only on push to main, so the first real execution of this wiring happens on the next main landing — a bad time to discover a contract mismatch. Adding a manual trigger lets you dispatch the stub on demand (on main it asserts the current head tree against the last SM validation, a harmless no-op when green):

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

This matches the sibling `factory-sm-kicker.yml`, which also exposes `workflow_dispatch` alongside its automatic triggers. On a `workflow_dispatch` event `github.event.head_commit.id` is empty and the canonical script falls back to `github.sha`, so the called guard handles this event shape correctly (verified in the live `factory-sm-merge-guard.yml`: `ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}`).

Purely optional — no impact on correctness.
